subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these 14 grouped action upgrades—including four credential-sensitive action families—after exact-SHA provenance and the rebased workflow gates are verified?
rationale: The code changes are mechanically narrow, but repository automation executes the new upstream code with app keys, registry credentials, repository tokens, and API credentials; only an authorized owner can accept that trust-boundary change.

options.title: Approve after provenance and gates
options.body: Verify all proposed SHAs against official immutable releases, refresh the branch, require the relevant security and workflow checks to pass, then approve the grouped update.

options.title: Split sensitive action updates
options.body: Separate app-token, Docker credential/build, and Codex-action updates from routine setup and maintenance actions for narrower review and rollback.

options.title: Hold the grouped update
options.body: Leave the PR open until Dependabot can rebase successfully and the dependency check plus remaining workflow checks complete on the exact head.

recommendation.title: Approve after provenance and gates
recommendation.body: Verify all proposed SHAs against official immutable releases, refresh the branch, require the relevant security and workflow checks to pass, then approve the grouped update.

likelyOwner.reason: The history and live timeline most strongly connect this person to repository-wide release, Docker, security-sensitive workflow, and operational decisions.
